messages:
marisa: kicking off kernel 6.3.9 canary to eu-west-2 ampere subset (40 nodes). will watch NCCL telem closely.
vik: when did the newer NVIDIA driver land on any of those hosts? mixed driver/kernel combos have bitten us before.
marisa: drivers are mixed. some hosts on 525.60, a few still on 515.86 due to package conflicts from last month.
cheng: quick checks to run on an affected host: `nvidia-smi topo -m`, `dmesg | egrep -i \"ACS|AER|peer access\"`, and `lspci -vv` for bridge details. ACS denial shows up in dmesg.
marisa: collected sample dmesg from node eu2-amp-07:
```
[  874.321] pcieport 0000:5e:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Severity: fatal)
[  874.322] pcieport 0000:5e:00.0: PCIe ACS: peer access disabled for 0000:5f:00.0
[  874.323] nvlink0: link negotiation failed, falling back to PCIe
```
\ncallum: ACS denial explains P2P drop. curious why only a subset of nodes after kernel bump though. BIOS/bridge firmware differences?
aisha: infra-cost-bot: cost-alert -> eu-west-2 ampere pool spotted a 38% increase in reserved capacity churn in the last 25m. projected burn +$7.2k/day if slow path persists :rotating_light:
vik: my hunch: kernel 6.3.9 tightened ACS/FLR enforcement, and with older driver kernels the NV driver probes different topology flags. mixed-state -> asymmetric view of bridges -> NVLink/P2P disabled -> NCCL falls back to TCP/PCIe and steps slow down.
marisa: repro plan: SSH to node, run `nvidia-smi topo -m`, `nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2` across two GPUs on different sockets, and check `dmesg` for AER/ACS.
oncall-rotation: acknowledged, taking ownership of canary pause. initiating rollback to kernel 6.2 on the canary subset now.
marisa: started cordon + drain for affected canary nodes; 8 nodes draining. will hold new kernel rollouts until investigation complete.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback queued -> kernel-6.2 -> target: eu-west-2/ampere-canary -> job_id: 0x9c3
vik: we should also standardize driver to 525.60 across the canary before reattempt. mixed 515/525 is a debugging nightmare.
cheng: adding a compatibility check to canary CI: kernel-driver topology test (runs `nvidia-smi topo -m` and simple NCCL perf) and firmware sanity (bridge flags).
marisa: rollback done on canary (8 nodes). quick verification: P2P restored on 7/8; one node still shows blocked.
callum: that remaining node likely has older IO-bridge firmware. scheduling a firmware push and a subsequent reboot.
aisha: cost update: autoscaler activity reduced, estimated return to baseline in ~35m. proactive drain policy saved ~ $5.8k/day relative to projected spike.
oncall-rotation: new directive -> hold kernel rollouts in eu-west-2 until: (1) drivers pinned to a single version in canary, (2) compatibility checks added to rollout pipeline, (3) ampere BIOS + bridge firmware audit completed.
marisa: action items:
- pin canary to kernel 6.2 while we stabilize (marisa)
- uniform driver rollout to 525.60 and add kernel-driver topo test to CI (vik + cheng)
- firmware/BIOS audit for eu-west-2 ampere nodes (callum)
- temporary drain policy for non-prod workloads in affected pools to avoid autoscaler churn (aisha)
- postmortem template + cluster telemetry snapshot for exec (oncall-rotation)

marisa: will update thread when metrics show normal P99 latencies and NCCL reports native P2P. closing after the post-rollback verification window (~45m).
